title: Romesco Sauce
subtitle: Catalan pepper, tomato, and almond sauce
excerpt: Romesco is a bold Spanish sauce from Catalonia, made from roasted peppers, tomato, almonds, and smoked paprika. It is served with grilled vegetables, fish, and the spring onion dish known as calots. This version uses anchovy for extra depth. It keeps well in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Romesco originates in Tarragona, Catalonia, where it was traditionally made by fishermen to eat with their catch. It is now used as a condiment across Spain and widely in restaurants worldwide.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: The breadcrumbs thicken and emulsify the sauce. Use slightly stale bread or dried breadcrumbs. The almonds can be toasted in a dry pan for extra flavour before adding.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Place the pepper halves and garlic cloves on a roasting tray. Drizzle with a little oil. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the peppers are soft and lightly charred.
Cool the peppers slightly. Peel off the skins. Squeeze the garlic out of its skin.
Put the roasted peppers, garlic, and tomatoes in a blender. Add the anchovy, breadcrumbs, sherry vinegar, smoked paprika, and chilli flakes.
Blend to a rough paste. With the motor running, drizzle in the olive oil until the sauce is smooth but still has some texture.
Season with salt. Taste and adjust with more vinegar or smoked paprika.

items.cause: Too many breadcrumbs or not enough oil
items.fix: Add more olive oil and blend again.
A little char on the peppers is what gives the sauce its depth. Do not over-protect them from the heat.

content.text: Romesco comes from Tarragona in Catalonia, where it was made by fishermen to serve with their catch. The sauce is central to the Catalan tradition of calotada -- a winter feast where spring onions are grilled over an open fire and eaten dipped in romesco. It is now used across Spain and internationally as a condiment for fish, meat, and roasted vegetables.
